source.title: Generalizing Motion Planners with Mixture of Experts for Autonomous Driving
source.authors: Qiao Sun; Huimin Wang; Jia-Hao Zhan; Fan Nie; Xin Wen; Lei-Meng Xu; Kun Zhan; Peng Jia; Xian-Peng Lang; Hang Zhao

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some table formatting is flattened, but the scaling-study plot is identified and described in the text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling relationships in autonomous-driving motion planning, a different domain and training regime from language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The LiAuto scaling experiment reports a log-log relationship between test loss and dataset size and model parameters. Other benchmark results are not recorded as scaling-law rows: they use different performance metrics, and Table V's flattened layout does not securely map all values to its four listed model names.
record.test_reason: Section IV-C trains STR2-CKS motion planners on LiAuto driving data across about 3 orders of magnitude in dataset size and over 2 in model size. It reports that converged test L2 loss follows a log-log (power-law) relation, with L(N) = (Nc/N)^αN. This is a new modality and training regime with a result on the power-law form, so it bears on V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly right. The authors' main conclusion, however, is that the MoE-based STR2 generalizes better than prior planners on NuPlan, including closed-loop and zero-shot InterPlan tests. The LiAuto scaling result, test loss following a log-log relationship with data and model size up to 1B samples, is a secondary claim. The authors defer a comprehensive scaling analysis with larger models to future work.
record.recipe_differences: This is an autonomous-driving motion-planning scaling study using trajectory L2 test loss and LiAuto data, rather than language-model pretraining loss and the original language-model scaling setup.
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation
record.problems: The LiAuto scaling-curve values are shown only in Fig. 3; numerical values and uncertainty estimates are not given in the text. The paper leaves larger-model scaling analysis for future work.
record.rows_left_out: Table V lists STR and several STR2 sizes with Val14 metrics, but the flattened table shows four model names and only three apparent sets of metric values, so values cannot be securely assigned. Those benchmark metrics also do not report a fitted scaling law.

untested.parts: Image and video models, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer. Scaling in compute is not tested, and no exponent values are given that could be compared with the language-model laws.
Not tested: the study has no language-model pretraining loss.
Not tested: there is no extrapolation from small fits to larger runs.
Not tested: there is no compute-optimal allocation analysis.
Not tested: there is no comparison of shape at fixed parameter count.
Not tested: downstream closed-loop scores are not related to scale or loss.
Not tested: there is no sensitivity analysis of the fits.

record.verdict_notes: The scaling evidence is a single figure plus a stated fit form, with no numeric exponents, uncertainties or goodness-of-fit. 'Dataset size' is described as tokens D in the Fig. 3 caption but as samples in the text. Table V (NuPlan open-loop metrics vs. model size) shows small, monotone gains but is not a power-law fit. Its values cannot be mapped to its four model names, as declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether fits on smaller runs predict loss on runs orders of magnitude larger.
Fixed-compute allocation between parameters and tokens and how the optimal allocation changes with compute.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
The study tests motion-planning scaling on the LiAuto dataset, but not image or video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Downstream-task performance as a function of pretraining loss or scale.
Sensitivity of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations to setup and fitting choices, and whether curves bend away from a power law.

relationships.condition: STR2-CKS MoE motion-planning models on the LiAuto dataset: data up to 1B samples, models up to 300M parameters
relationships.reason: Authors report that test L2 loss scales log-log with dataset size and with parameters, fitted as L(N) = (Nc/N)^αN (R1, R2). The support is weak: figure-only, with no exponent or fit quality reported.
relationships.display_finding: Test L2 loss showed log-log scaling with dataset size and parameters, with a reported parameter fit L(N)=(Nc/N)^αN but no numerical exponent or fit quality.
